==English==
{{wp}}
[[File:Prostitute tj.jpg|thumb|A '''prostitute''' in [[Tijuana]], [[Mexico]].]]

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*per-|id1=before||*steh₂-}}
{{ety|en|:der|la:prōstitūtus|tree=1}}
From {{der|en|la|prōstitūtus}}, past participle of {{m|la|prōstituō}}, from {{af|la|prō̆|t1=for, before|statuō|t2=to set up, to erect|nocat=1}}.

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɒstɪˌtjuːt/|[ˈpɹɒstɪtʰjuːt]|a=RP,non-yod-coalescence}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɒstɪˌt͡ʃuːt/|[ˈpɹɒstɪˌt͡ʃuːt]|a=yod-coalescence}}
* {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɑstɪˌtu(ː)t/|[ˈpɹɑstɪˌtʰu(ː)t]|a=GA,[[w:weak vowel merger|without weak vowel merger]]}}
** {{IPA|en|/ˈpɹɑstəˌtu(ː)t/|a=[[w:weak vowel merger|weak vowel merger]]}}
*** {{audio|en|en-us-prostitute.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyph|en|pros|ti|tute}}

===Adjective===
{{en-adj}}

# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[debased|Debased]], [[corrupt]]; seeking personal gain by dishonourable means. {{defdate|16th–19th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Paine Rights of Man|passage=[H]e speaks a languages that merits not reply, and which can only excite contempt for his '''prostitute''' principles, or pity for his ignorance.}}
# Taking part in [[promiscuous]] sexual activity, [[licentious]]; {{i|later, chiefly as attributive use of noun}} that is a prostitute. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
#* {{quote-journal|en|year=2008|author=Niki Adams; Lisa Longstaff|journal=The Guardian|section=letters, 23 February
|passage=They rightly say that attacks against '''prostitute''' women are common and that it's only when five are murdered in one place that it starts to provoke debate.}}
# {{lb|en|obsolete}} [[exposed|Exposed]], [[subjected]] ({{m|en|to}} something shameful). {{defdate|16th–18th c.}}
#* {{RQ:Hobbes Government|chapter=Reader|page=28|passage=[A]nd novv at length all men of all Nations, not only Philoſophers, but even the vulgar, have, and doe ſtill deale vvith this {{quote-gloss|the subject of the book}} as a matter of eaſe, expoſed and '''proſtitute''' to every Mother-vvit, and to be attained vvithout any great care or ſtudy, {{...}}}}

===Noun===
{{en-noun}}

# Any [[person]] (especially a [[woman]]) who has [[sexual intercourse]] or engages in other [[sexual]] activity for [[payment]], especially as a means of livelihood. {{defdate|from 18th c.}}
#: {{syn|en|sex worker|Thesaurus:prostitute}}
#: {{hypo|en|Thesaurus:prostitute}}
# {{rfd-sense|en}} A [[woman]] who has [[sexual intercourse]] or engages in other [[sexual]] activity for [[payment]], especially as a means of livelihood. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|year=2012|author=Kelly Olson|title=Dress and the Roman Woman: Self-Presentation and Society|page=50
|passage=Unfortunately, there is to my knowledge no visual evidence for the dress of the Roman '''prostitute''', but the literary sources present us with a range of prostitute clothing (from rich accoutrements all the way down to nothing), {{...}}}}
# A person who does, or offers to do, a demeaning or dishonourable activity for [[money]] or personal gain; someone who acts in a dishonourable way for personal advantage. {{defdate|from 17th c.}}
#: {{syn|en|sellout}}
#* {{RQ:Independent|author=Jack Shepherd|quotee=Bobby Gillespie|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/eurovision-madonna-israel-bobby-gillespie-tel-aviv-primal-scream-a8919486.html|title=Primal Scream frontman calls Madonna a 'total prostitute' for performing at Eurovision in Israel|date=2019-05-18|passage=Madonna would do anything for money, you know, she's a total '''prostitute'''. And I've got nothing against prostitutes.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20240417072226/https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/tv/news/eurovision-madonna-israel-bobby-gillespie-tel-aviv-primal-scream-a8919486.html|archivedate=17 April 2024}}

====Usage notes====
* Some speakers consider prostitutes (sex workers) to be female by default, and thus use ''male prostitute'' to refer to a male performing the same job.

====Synonyms====
* [[Thesaurus:prostitute]]

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive|reflexive}} To offer (oneself or someone else) for [[sexual]] [[activity]] in exchange for [[money]]. {{defdate|from 16th c.}}
#* {{RQ:KJV|Leviticus|xix|29|passage=Do not '''prostitute''' thy daughter.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|derogatory}} To sacrifice (oneself, one's talents etc.) in return for profit or other advantage; to [[exploit]] for base purposes.
#* {{quote-book|en|author=w:John Dyer|chapter=The Ruins of Rome. A Poem.|title=Poems. [...] Viz. I. Grongar Hill. II. The Ruins of Rome. III. The Fleece, in Four Books|location=London|publisher=Printed by John Hughs, for Messrs. [[w:Robert Dodsley|R[obert]]] and [[w:James Dodsley|J[ames] Dodsley]],{{nb...|in Pallmall.}}|year=1740|year_published=1759|pages=42–43|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=A0gVAAAAQAAJ&pg=PA42|oclc=991281870|passage=[T]heſe, their rights / In the vile ſtreets they '''proſtitute''' to ſale; / Their ancient rights, their dignities, their laws, / Their native glorious freedom.}}
